content:
Yesterday we saw the male goat as the sin offering; the animal of the Day of Atonement, bearing sin on behalf of the whole congregation, going outside the camp to the place of rejection, pointing to Christ who was made sin for us and crucified outside the gate. Today we look at one of the most significant details of the sin offering in Numbers 7: there was only one. While the peace offerings included many animals two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs and the burnt offering included three animals, the sin offering was a single male goat.
Just one. Every tribe, every leader, every day; one goat. Why?

To feel the full weight of the one goat, we need to set it next to the peace offerings that accompanied it. Each tribal leader brought two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs for the peace offerings. That is seventeen animals for peace, fellowship, and celebration before Yahweh. Abundance. Variety. Many animals, many expressions, many dimensions of the restored relationship between the people and their God. But for the sin offering; one goat. The contrast is not accidental. The peace offerings are many because there are many ways to express the joy of fellowship with God and many dimensions of what that fellowship means, such as: abundance, celebration, fellowship and more. But the sin offering is one because there is only one way to deal with sin. Sin cannot be handled from many angles. It cannot be addressed by accumulation. One substitute. One bearing. One removal.

This contrast anticipates one of the most clear and direct statements in all of Paul’s writing. In 1 Timothy 2:5 he says: “For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.” One mediator. Not one among several. Not one who works alongside others. One. The many animals of the peace offering speak of the many expressions of worship that can rise before God; singing, prayer, service, giving, fellowship, feasting together in His presence. All of these are the peace offering’s abundance. But the one goat of the sin offering says that all of this rich fellowship, all of this many-sided worship, rests on a single atoning act. Remove the one goat and the seventeen peace offering animals have no foundation to stand on. Remove Christ’s one sacrifice and all the worship of the world is weightless.

The writer of Hebrews labours over this singularity more than any other New Testament writer. In Hebrews 10:11-12 he draws the sharpest possible contrast: “Every priest stands daily at his service, offering repeatedly the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins. But when Christ had offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.” Every priest stands. Christ sat down. The standing priest is still working because the offering is incomplete. The sitting Christ is finished because the offering is complete. The one goat was offered again and again every year at every feast, every new moon, every Day of Atonement; always pointing, never completing. The one sacrifice of Christ sat down because there is nothing left to offer. It is finished.

Hebrews 9:28 says: “Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many.” Once. Not twice for good measure. Not once for each generation that comes after. Once; and the once reaches forward to cover every generation that will ever live, backward to cover every generation that had already lived, and outward to cover every tribe and people and nation that has ever existed. The one goat of Numbers 7 was given to show that when the true sin offering comes, once will be enough. One sacrifice sufficient for all, for all time, for all sin, for all who will come through it.

There is a deeper reason why the sin offering was only one, and it goes to the very nature of what sin is. The peace offerings were many because peace can be expressed in many dimensions; between individuals, between communities, between man and God, in gratitude, in celebration, in covenant renewal, in everyday fellowship. Peace has many facets. But sin has one root. Romans 5:12 says: “Therefore, just as sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because all sinned.” Sin entered through one act, by one man, through one broken obedience. The entire river of human sinfulness has one source. And because sin has one source, the answer to sin is one sacrifice.

This is what made the sacrificial system of Israel so radical in the ancient world. Every religion around Israel multiplied its offerings in the hope that more would be more effective. More gods, more sacrifices, more rituals, more accumulation. But Yahweh gave Israel one sin offering because He was pointing toward the one true atonement that would make all the accumulation unnecessary. One goat said: the answer to sin is not quantity. The answer to sin is the right one. And John 1:29 gives us the identification: “Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.” Not the sins in parts, not sin in one generation, not sin in one nation. The sin of the world; the whole root, the whole river, the whole reality of what entered through Adam; taken away by one offering.

For the new creation believer, the one goat of the sin offering carries both a comfort and a call. The comfort is this: you do not need to keep bringing more sin offerings. The one has been given. Hebrews 10:14 says: “For by a single offering He has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.” Perfected. For all time. You are not standing before God as someone whose sin is partially dealt with, waiting for more offerings to cover the remainder. The one goat is sufficient for everything you have done and everything you will yet do. You stand before Yahweh in the full covering of the one sufficient sacrifice.

The call is equally clear: do not treat the one as though it needs supplementing.
There is nothing to add to the sin offering of Christ. No amount of personal effort, religious performance, or accumulated good behaviour adds anything to the one goat. 1 John 1:7 says: “The blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.” All sin. The one goat was brought for the whole tribe. The whole tribe was covered. Every person in it not the ones who brought enough additional offerings but every person sheltered under the one. This is the message the twelve tribal leaders were declaring one by one over twelve days as they each placed their single male goat before the altar: we need one. We have one. One is enough.

title: Prayer
text:
Yahweh, how great are Your works; Your thoughts are very deep (Psalm 92:5).
We thank You for the one goat; for the deliberate, intentional singularity of the sin offering that has been pointing to the one true atoning sacrifice from the day the first goat was placed on the altar. We thank You that Christ sat down because the work is finished, that the one offering has perfected for all time those who are His, and that we do not stand before You waiting for more to be added to what He gave. Forgive us for the times we have behaved as though the one were not enough; as though our guilt required more than He paid, as though our sin had somehow exceeded what the sin offering covers. It has not. The one goat is sufficient. The blood of Jesus cleanses from all sin. Help us to rest in the one, to stop reaching for more offerings to lay alongside it, and to live today as people who are fully, permanently, and completely covered by the single sacrifice that sat down at the right hand of God and finished the work forever. In Christ’s name, amen.
